record.original_question: Does there exist a model of computation for which the Invariance Theorem remains valid for time complexity as well?

evidence.quote: Is there any model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem holds true also for the time complexity? (C. Calude)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Fix a class of computational models $\mathcal{M}$ (for instance, Turing machines with a finite tape alphabet and a fixed input/output convention). For a model $M \in \mathcal{M}$ and a finite binary string $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, let
\[
C_M(x) = \min\{|p| : p \in \{0,1\}^*,\ M(p) = x\}
\]
denote the description complexity of $x$ relative to $M$. The Invariance Theorem of algorithmic information theory asserts that there exists a model $U \in \mathcal{M}$ (a universal model) such that for every $M \in \mathcal{M}$ there is a constant $c_{U,M}$ with
\[
C_U(x) \le C_M(x) + c_{U,M} \quad \text{for all } x \in \{0,1\}^*.
\]
Now let $\mathrm{time}_M(p)$ denote the number of computation steps of $M$ on input $p$, and define a time-complexity analogue
\[
T_M(x) = \min\{\mathrm{time}_M(p) : M(p) = x\}.
\]

Question. Does there exist a class $\mathcal{M}$ of computational models and a distinguished "universal" model $U \in \mathcal{M}$ such that the Invariance Theorem holds for the time-complexity measure $T_M$, in the sense that for every $M \in \mathcal{M}$ there exists a constant $c_{U,M}$ (independent of $x$) with
\[
T_U(x) \le T_M(x) + c_{U,M} \quad \text{for all } x \in \{0,1\}^*,
\]
(or, more generally, $T_U(x) \le T_M(x) + O(1)$ rather than the multiplicative or logarithmic overhead typical of universal simulation)?
artifact.category_tag: algorithmic information theory / time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to C. Calude in a list of open problems in algorithmic information theory, asks whether the Invariance Theorem (which holds for plain Kolmogorov complexity up to an additive constant) can be made to hold for time complexity in some model of computation. Standard universal-simulation results introduce multiplicative or logarithmic time overhead, and no source found in the search explicitly resolves Calude's question; available references continue to list it as an open problem with no definitive solution identified.

status_evidence.snippet: Is there any model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem holds true also for the time complexity? (C. Calude)
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem in algorithmic information theory.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The invariance theorem states that for any two universal description languages U1, U2, |C_{U1}(x) - C_{U2}(x)| <= c, but standard universal simulation incurs multiplicative or logarithmic time overhead.
status_evidence.claim: Classical invariance is additive for description length, but no constant-overhead invariance is known for time.
